question: Explain the concept of permanent establishment (PE) under tax treaties and its significance for taxing the business profits of a non-resident enterprise.
sources: OECD Model Tax Convention on Income and on Capital, Articles 5 and 7
UN Model Double Taxation Convention, Articles 5 and 7

points.label: Significance of PE
points.description: Under the business profits article, profits of an enterprise are taxable only in its country of residence unless it carries on business in the other country through a PE there; the other country may then tax only the profits attributable to that PE.

points.label: Fixed place PE
points.description: A fixed place of business through which the business is wholly or partly carried on, such as a place of management, branch, office, factory, workshop, or a mine or other place of extracting natural resources; the Income-tax Act also defines PE in these terms for transfer pricing and treaty purposes.
points.basis: Model Tax Conventions, Article 5(1) and (2); Income-tax Act, 1961, section 92F(iiia)

points.label: Construction and service PE
points.description: A building site or construction, installation or assembly project is a PE only if it lasts longer than the period set in the treaty; many Indian treaties also treat services furnished through employees in the other country beyond a set number of days as a PE.
points.basis: Model Tax Conventions, Article 5(3) (UN Model includes service PE)

points.label: Preparatory or auxiliary activities
points.description: Activities such as storage, display, purchasing goods or collecting information do not create a PE where they are only preparatory or auxiliary; anti-fragmentation rules stop splitting activities to fit this exception.

points.label: Agency PE
points.description: A dependent agent who habitually concludes contracts, or plays the principal role leading to contracts, on behalf of the enterprise creates a PE; an independent agent acting in the ordinary course of its own business does not.
